strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses genuine limitations of existing multi-objective GFlowNet approaches requiring retraining or auxiliary classifiers
Solid theoretical contribution: Proposition 4.1 rigorously proves exact recovery of target distribution for linear scalarization with complete proofs
Unified framework: elegantly handles both scalarization and logical operators under one method, unlike prior work addressing them separately

Comprehensive experimental validation: synthetic experiments with computable ground truth (L1 error), real-world molecule generation across multiple settings with both scalarization and logical operators
Significant efficiency gains: 40-70× speedup over classifier-guided approaches with superior molecular validity (99.6-99.8% vs 54.8-86.8%)
Good ablation study: ensemble baseline effectively validates the importance of reaching probability weighting
Clear presentation: well-motivated problem setup, clear method exposition, extensive appendices supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty of core contribution: the weighting scheme by reaching probability u(s)=F(s)/Z_i is straightforward application of existing GFlowNet machinery rather than a novel technical insight

Significant theoretical gaps for non-linear operators: while linear scalarization is proved exact, common cases (β≠1) and logical operators only receive empirical analysis through distortion factor visualization; claim to 'quantify approximation quality' overstates delivery as no theoretical bounds or rates are provided

Mixed experimental results on real benchmarks: Table 3 shows HN-GFN achieves higher rewards on several objectives; Table 4 shows variable performance across logical operator compositions; improvements described as 'comparable' rather than clearly superior

Practical limitation inadequately discussed: correlated rewards cause contrast operator to fail (Table A6, Fig A7), a significant constraint for real applications relegated to appendix rather than main text discussion

Non-negligible inference overhead for scalarization: 1.5-2× slower than baselines (Table 5: 23-46ms vs 15-32ms) contradicts 'minimal overhead' framing in paper, and trade-off between training and inference cost not thoroughly analyzed
Limited compatibility with GFlowNet training objectives: method requires learned state flow F(s), incompatible with Trajectory Balance objective, restricting applicability
Missing sensitivity analyses: no ablation on β values despite it being a key hyperparameter; no study of robustness to errors in learned F(s) and Z_i estimates
Narrow experimental scope: evaluation limited to 2D grid and molecular generation despite motivation mentioning proteins and sequences; generalization to other domains unvalidated

Incomplete distortion factor analysis: visualization shows δ(x) approximately constant in high-density regions for non-linear cases (Fig. 3) but this is empirical observation without formalization or error bounds

strengths: Strong theoretical result: Proposition 4.1 proves exact recovery for linear scalarization (β=1) with rigorous proofs structured across supporting lemmas
Unifying framework that handles both scalarization and logical operators, unlike prior work addressing only one formulation
Practical compatibility with all standard GFlowNet training objectives via two routes for computing reaching probabilities (Model F and DB F)
Comprehensive empirical validation on both synthetic domain (2D grid with ground-truth distributions) and real-world molecular generation tasks
Significant computational efficiency: 30-65× speedup for logical operators compared to classifier-guided composition at inference time
Insightful approximation quality analysis (Section 5.3, Figure 3) showing distortion factor remains approximately constant in high-density regions
Well-structured presentation with clear motivation, comprehensive appendix, and reproducible experimental details across multiple seeds and metrics
weaknesses: Theoretical guarantees limited to linear scalarization with β=1; for general nonlinear operators and β≠1, approximation quality lacks theoretical bounds despite empirical validation
Temperature parameter handling appears ad-hoc: β=32 used in real experiments but theory assumes β=1; reward-sharpened mixing policy (Eq. 31) introduced late with insufficient justification

Contrast operator exhibits systematic failures with positively correlated objectives (Table A9: pQED⊗pGAP achieves 52% vs. 73% for uncorrelated pairs), limiting applicability without clear guidance on when to avoid
Inference overhead of 8-40ms per sample for scalarization is non-negligible compared to preference-conditioned baselines, potentially problematic for time-sensitive applications
Missing critical sensitivity analyses: no evaluation of robustness to poorly trained base models, inaccurate partition functions, or weak backward policies required by DB F route
Requires training individual base GFlowNet for each single objective first, meaning substantial upfront investment not eliminated—method only avoids retraining during composition
Limited scalability evaluation: maximum 5 objectives tested; no complexity analysis or discussion of behavior with large state spaces or many objectives

Real-world results show modest improvements over baselines with high variance (e.g., Table 3 SEH-QED diversity 0.564-0.565 vs. 0.568-0.571 baseline; Table 4 QM9 GAP-QED: 0.636-0.655 ours vs. 0.642-0.665 MOGFN)

strengths: Addresses practical problem of composing pre-trained GFlowNets without retraining, which is a genuine limitation of existing methods
Provides clean theoretical result (Proposition 4.1) proving exact recovery for linear scalarization with β=1
Unified framework handling both linear scalarization and nonlinear logical operators, more general than prior work
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablations, detailed appendices, and reproducible setup
Significant inference speedup for logical operators (30-65× faster than classifier-guided composition)
Thoughtful analysis of distortion factor for nonlinear operators, showing it remains approximately constant in high-density regions
weaknesses: Critical gap between theory and practice: main theoretical result (Proposition 4.1) applies only to β=1, but real experiments use β=32 where no exactness guarantees hold; approximation quality for β≠1 analyzed only empirically with no formal bounds

Empirical improvements are marginal and inconsistent: molecular generation results (Tables 3-5) show results often within noise of baselines or sometimes worse; undermines practical value of the contribution
Significant inference overhead (8-40ms per sample, 50-150% increase over baselines) contradicts main advantage of avoiding retraining; substantially increases generation time in practice

Limited understanding of failure modes: method fails with correlated rewards (Tables A9, A8, Fig. A8) but this critical limitation is relegated to appendix with minimal discussion; no principled guidance on when method will succeed vs. fail

Core technical novelty is limited: using reaching probabilities as composition weights is relatively straightforward once conceived; contribution is recognizing and applying existing quantity rather than developing new techniques

Non-constant distortion factor δ(x) for nonlinear operators deviates from target, with deviations dismissed as 'contributing minimally' without rigorous justification; unclear when approximation becomes problematic

Experimental design choices not justified: β=32 for molecules seems arbitrarily high; no sensitivity analysis on temperature parameter despite varying β across settings; missing comparison with simple baselines
Incomplete analysis of reaching probability computation costs: Model F requires explicit flow parameterization; DB F requires backward policy; no detailed overhead comparison between routes
